patterns.message: The shared kernel’s domain holds identifiers and event plumbing, and depends on nothing else.
The shared kernel’s application layer holds the ports and faults every context shares, and depends only on the shared kernel.
The platform is technical plumbing shared by every context; it knows no bounded context.
Work’s domain depends on itself, the shared kernel’s domain, and the published language of other contexts.
Work’s application layer depends on its own domain, the shared kernel, and what other contexts publish. Reach anything else through a port under @work/application/ports.
Work’s infrastructure implements its own ports. It may not reach another context’s internals; take what it needs through a published port.
Work’s presentation drives its own application layer, and uses other contexts only through what they publish.
Work’s module wires its own parts to the platform, the shared kernel and to what other contexts publish; it never reaches their adapters or internals.
